# sysutils_package_repository (Resource)

Manages an OS package repository, the companion of `sysutils_package`: for apt, a deb822 file `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/<name>.sources`; for dnf and yum, a file `/etc/yum.repos.d/<name>.repo`; for apk, a line in `/etc/apk/repositories`, after a comment line naming the repository. A signing key, given inline or fetched from a URL, is stored ASCII-armored in `/etc/apt/keyrings/<name>.asc` (apt) or `/etc/pki/rpm-gpg/RPM-GPG-KEY-<name>` (dnf and yum). Files are written atomically with mode `0644`, owned by `root`, below the provider's `root_dir` if that is set, and removed on destroy. Refresh reads them back, so changes made outside Terraform show up as a planned change of `content` or `signing_key_sha256`. Requires root privileges.

It covers the same ground as Ansible's `deb822_repository`, `yum_repository` and the repository handling of `apk`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Docker's apt repository, with its key fetched from Docker and stored in
# /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc. The package index is refreshed after every
# change, so the package below can be installed right away.
resource "sysutils_package_repository" "docker" {
  name            = "docker"
  description     = "Docker CE"
  uris            = ["https://download.docker.com/linux/debian"]
  suites          = ["bookworm"]
  components      = ["stable"]
  architectures   = ["amd64"]
  signing_key_url = "https://download.docker.com/linux/debian/gpg"
  refresh_cache   = true
}

resource "sysutils_package" "docker" {
  name = "docker-ce"

  depends_on = [sysutils_package_repository.docker]
}

# A dnf repository whose key dnf fetches itself. dnf variables such as
# $releasever are passed through.
resource "sysutils_package_repository" "pgdg" {
  name            = "pgdg16"
  manager         = "dnf"
  description     = "PostgreSQL 16 for Fedora $releasever"
  uris            = ["https://download.postgresql.org/pub/repos/yum/16/fedora/fedora-$releasever-$basearch"]
  signing_key_url = "https://download.postgresql.org/pub/repos/yum/keys/PGDG-RPM-GPG-KEY-Fedora"
}

# A local flat apt repository, signed by a key kept next to the
# configuration.
resource "sysutils_package_repository" "local" {
  name        = "local"
  manager     = "apt"
  uris        = ["file:///srv/apt"]
  suites      = ["./"]
  signing_key = file("${path.module}/local-repo.asc")
}

# Alpine's edge/testing repository, tagged so that only packages asked for
# as "name@testing" come from it.
resource "sysutils_package_repository" "alpine_testing" {
  name    = "testing"
  manager = "apk"
  uris    = ["https://dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org/alpine/edge/testing"]
  tag     = "testing"
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the repository, such as `"docker"`: the file name without extension for apt, dnf and yum, and the dnf repository id. Letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-`, starting with a letter or digit, at most 100 bytes. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `uris` (List of String) Base URLs of the repository: apt's `URIs`, dnf's `baseurl`, the apk repository. `http`, `https` and `file` URLs only, without white space, `#` or credentials; apk takes exactly one. dnf variables such as `$releasever` and `$basearch` are passed through.

### Optional

- `architectures` (List of String) apt only: architectures to download indexes for, such as `["amd64"]`. If unset, apt uses all configured architectures.
- `components` (List of String) apt only: components, such as `["main", "contrib"]`. Required unless the suite is the path of a flat repository.
- `description` (String) Human-readable name of the repository: dnf's `name` (which defaults to `name`), `X-Repolib-Name` for apt, and part of the comment line for apk. A single line of at most 256 bytes.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the package manager uses the repository: `Enabled: no` for apt, `enabled=0` for dnf and yum, a commented-out line for apk. Defaults to `true`.
- `gpg_check` (Boolean) dnf and yum only: whether package signatures are checked (`gpgcheck`). Defaults to `true`; `false` is refused for apt and apk, which have no such per-repository switch.
- `manager` (String) Package manager whose repository to manage: `"apt"`, `"dnf"`, `"yum"` or `"apk"`. `"auto"` uses apt if `/etc/apt` is a directory, else dnf or yum if one of `/etc/yum.repos.d`, `/etc/dnf` and `/etc/yum` is, else apk if `/etc/apk` is, looking below `root_dir` if that is set. Defaults to `"auto"`. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `refresh_cache` (Boolean) Refresh the package index (`apt-get update`, `dnf makecache`, `yum makecache` or `apk update`) after the repository was created, changed or removed, so that `sysutils_package` resources that depend on this one find its packages. A failed refresh fails the apply and is retried by the next one. Not supported with `root_dir`, since it would refresh the host's index. Defaults to `false`.
- `signing_key` (String) ASCII-armored OpenPGP public key that signs the repository (apt) or its packages (dnf, yum), stored in `signing_key_path` and referred to by `Signed-By` or `gpgkey`. Conflicts with `signing_key_url`. Not supported for apk, whose keys must be named after their signer.
- `signing_key_url` (String) `https` or `file` URL of the OpenPGP public key. For apt, the provider fetches the key during apply, converts a binary (`.gpg`) key to ASCII armor and stores it in `signing_key_path`; a `file` URL is read from the host, as `root_dir` does not apply to it. The key is fetched again when the URL changes or the stored key no longer matches what was fetched, not when the key behind the URL changes. For dnf and yum, the URL is written to `gpgkey` as is, and dnf fetches it itself. Plain `http` is refused, since anyone on the network path could replace the key. Conflicts with `signing_key`.
- `suites` (List of String) apt only, and required for apt: suites or codenames, such as `["bookworm"]`. A suite ending with `/` is the path of a flat repository, such as `["./"]`, and takes no `components`.
- `tag` (String) apk only: tag of the repository, written as `@tag` before the URL. Packages from a tagged repository are only installed when asked for as `name@tag`. 1 to 64 letters, digits, `_` or `-`.
- `types` (List of String) apt only: `"deb"` and/or `"deb-src"`. Defaults to `["deb"]`.

### Read-Only

- `content` (String) Contents of the repository file, or, for apk, the managed lines of `/etc/apk/repositories`. Refresh reads them back, so any change made outside Terraform shows up as a planned change of this attribute; a file with another mode or owner reads as null.
- `id` (String) Resource identifier (equal to `name`).
- `path` (String) Path of the repository file: `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/<name>.sources`, `/etc/yum.repos.d/<name>.repo` or `/etc/apk/repositories`.
- `signing_key_path` (String) Path of the stored signing key: `/etc/apt/keyrings/<name>.asc` or `/etc/pki/rpm-gpg/RPM-GPG-KEY-<name>`; null if no key is stored.
- `signing_key_sha256` (String) SHA-256 of the stored signing key, as written (ASCII-armored). A key file changed, removed or given another mode or owner outside Terraform shows up as a change of this attribute.

## Files

| `manager` | Repository | Signing key | Refreshed with |
|-----------|------------|-------------|----------------|
| `apt` | `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/<name>.sources`, a [deb822](https://manpages.debian.org/stable/apt/sources.list.5.en.html) stanza with `Types`, `URIs`, `Suites`, `Components`, `Architectures`, `Signed-By` and `Enabled` | `/etc/apt/keyrings/<name>.asc` | `apt-get update` |
| `dnf`, `yum` | `/etc/yum.repos.d/<name>.repo`, section `[<name>]` with `name`, `baseurl`, `enabled`, `gpgcheck` and `gpgkey` | `/etc/pki/rpm-gpg/RPM-GPG-KEY-<name>` (inline keys only) | `dnf makecache`, `yum makecache` |
| `apk` | Two lines in `/etc/apk/repositories`: `# sysutils_package_repository <name>[: <description>]`, then `[#][@<tag> ]<uri>` | not supported | `apk update` |

With `manager = "auto"`, the default, the family is detected from the configuration directories: `/etc/apt`, then `/etc/yum.repos.d`, `/etc/dnf` or `/etc/yum`, then `/etc/apk`, below `root_dir` if that is set. For `refresh_cache`, `"auto"` uses `dnf` if it is installed and `yum` otherwise.

The `.sources`, `.repo` and key files are owned by `root` and have mode `0644`, so that apt's unprivileged `_apt` user can read the key. They are written atomically: to a temporary file in the same directory that gets its mode and owner first and is then renamed into place. The resource never takes over an existing file on create; import it instead. `/etc/apk/repositories` keeps its own mode, owner and other lines; only the two managed lines are changed.

## Signing Keys

`signing_key` takes an ASCII-armored OpenPGP public key, and `signing_key_url` an `https` or `file` URL of one, armored or binary (a `.gpg` keyring as Debian ships them in `/usr/share/keyrings`). The provider checks that the data is an OpenPGP public key, not a secret key or anything else, and stores it ASCII-armored, converting binary keys, which both apt (as a `.asc` keyring) and rpm accept. `signing_key_sha256` is the SHA-256 of the stored file.

- For apt, the key is stored in `/etc/apt/keyrings/<name>.asc` and the repository refers to it with `Signed-By`, so that it only vouches for this repository, not for every repository as a key in `/etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d` would.
- For dnf and yum, an inline key is stored in `/etc/pki/rpm-gpg/RPM-GPG-KEY-<name>` and referred to as `gpgkey=file:///etc/pki/rpm-gpg/RPM-GPG-KEY-<name>`; a `signing_key_url` is written to `gpgkey` unchanged, and dnf imports the key on first use.
- apk keys are not supported: apk finds a key by the name of its signer, so it must be installed under that name in `/etc/apk/keys`, for example with [`sysutils_file`](./file.md).

A key from `signing_key_url` is fetched during apply, never during plan, with a one-minute timeout and a 1 MiB limit. Redirects must stay on `https`. It is fetched again when the URL changes, or when the stored key file was changed, removed or given another mode or owner; a key that changes behind an unchanged URL is not noticed. Plain `http` is refused, since anyone on the network path could replace the key and with it every package from the repository. A `file` URL is read on the host running Terraform; `root_dir` does not apply to it.

## Validation

- `name` must match `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$` and be at most 100 bytes long: apt silently ignores files in `sources.list.d` with other characters in their names.
- `uris` must be `http`, `https` or `file` URLs with a lowercase scheme, without white space, control characters or `#`, and without credentials, which would end up in a world-readable file; configure credentials in `/etc/apt/auth.conf.d` or the repository's dnf options instead. `http` and `https` URLs need a host, `file` URLs an absolute path. dnf's `baseurl` separates URLs by commas, so they must not contain `,` there. apk takes exactly one URI.
- `suites`, `components`, `architectures` and `types` only apply to apt, and `suites` and, unless a suite ends with `/`, `components` are required there. `tag` only applies to apk, and `gpg_check = false` only to dnf and yum.
- `description` must be a single line.

Every value is written on a single line of its own, so no value can add another field, section or repository line to the file. Rules that depend on the package manager are checked during plan once the manager is known.

## Drift Detection

Refresh reads the files back. `content` is set to what the repository file contains (for apk, to the two managed lines), and `signing_key_sha256` to the SHA-256 of the stored key; a file with another mode or owner reads as null. Anything that differs from what the configuration would write, such as an edited URL, an added field or a replaced key, shows up as a change of these attributes and is reverted by the next apply. A repository file or managed line that was removed shows up as a repository to create.

## Refreshing the Package Index

With `refresh_cache = true`, the package index is refreshed after the repository or its key was created, changed or removed, so that [`sysutils_package`](./package.md) resources that depend on the repository find its packages. It runs under the same lock as `sysutils_package`, and counts as the once-per-run refresh of its `update_cache`. Without `refresh_cache`, a change still makes the next `sysutils_package` with `update_cache = true` refresh the index again, even if another one already did in the same run.

If the refresh fails, for example because the repository is unreachable, the apply fails, the repository stays written, and the next apply retries the refresh. On destroy, a failed refresh is only a warning.

`refresh_cache` is refused with the provider's `root_dir`, since it would refresh the index of the running host rather than of the tree.

## Import

A repository can be imported by name, or by `<manager>:<name>` to select the package manager:

```shell
# By name, with the package manager detected as for manager = "auto".
terraform import sysutils_package_repository.docker docker

# With an explicit package manager: <manager>:<name>.
terraform import sysutils_package_repository.alpine_testing apk:testing
```

Every attribute is read from the files: for apt, a `Signed-By` of `/etc/apt/keyrings/<name>.asc` imports that key as `signing_key`; for dnf and yum, a `gpgkey` of `file:///etc/pki/rpm-gpg/RPM-GPG-KEY-<name>` does, and any other `gpgkey` URL is imported as `signing_key_url`. `refresh_cache` is imported as `false`. A file written by other tools usually differs from what the resource writes, at least in its header comment, so the first apply after an import rewrites it.

## Caveats

- The resource requires root, unless `root_dir` points to a tree the user can write.
- For apt, a repository must not repeat the URI and suite of another source with a different `Signed-By`: apt refuses to use either then.
- Only the options above are managed. For others, such as dnf's `module_hotfixes` or apt pinning, use [`sysutils_ini_value`](./ini_value.md) or [`sysutils_file`](./file.md).
- Legacy one-line `.list` files are not managed, but can be replaced: remove the `.list` file and let this resource write a `.sources` file.
